text:
Maya: Heads up — during the sampleapp onboarding I noticed rotation breaks when both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY are present. SDK keeps using the old key for background streams. Anyone seen this?

Jon: Repro steps? what ordering and env changes did you do?

Maya: I started the app with REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_abc and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj_123. Then I rotated the project key in the container with `export REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=new_proj_456`. Non-stream requests pick up the new key but long-lived streams still use org_abc and start returning 401s.

Samir: Can you paste a short log snippet? sounds like the streaming client might cache the token at init and not re-read env after rotation.

Maya: Logs: `info auth: using key org_abc`, then `WARN stream: request failed 401`, then again `info auth: using key org_abc` (should have been new_proj_456).

Leah: FYI current SDK fallback precedence is: explicit param > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY > REDWOOD_API_KEY > ~/.redwood/credentials. We had a half-finished change to flip something here a while back.

Maya: In our case REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY is present and updated, so it should've been used. The puzzling part is why the running process kept using the old org key.

Jon: Most likely the streaming connection calls `auth.get_token()` once on connect and caches headers. If you change env vars in-process the client won't re-read them unless you explicitly force refresh or reconnect.

Samir: Right — streaming reuses an AuthState object. Quick fixes: 1) on SIGUSR1/SIGHUP trigger a reload of env-backed provider, 2) call `get_token(force_refresh=True)` before each reconnect. Longer-term: make the provider reactive.

Maya: Repro steps I used: 1) start sampleapp with org key, 2) `kubectl exec` into pod and `export REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=new_proj_456`, 3) hit the streaming endpoint and observe 401s. Will add exact steps to the bug.

Leah: Also a DX issue: when both envs exist we don't clearly log which one we chose. Could add an explicit startup info line showing resolved auth source and a dev-mode warning when org/project keys differ.

Jon: Agreed — a small startup message would avoid a lot of confusion. E.g. `Resolving auth: using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (proj_123) — REDWOOD_API_KEY present but deprioritized`.

DevExBot: Created issue #4321: "streaming client ignores env rotations; env precedence surprising" — assigned to @Samir.

Samir: I'll open a WIP PR: (a) make streaming client refresh token on reconnect, (b) add `REDWOOD_AUTH_PREFERENCE` env to let power users force `project|org|file`, (c) add startup warning when multiple keys are present. Will link tests.

Maya: Test plan: start sampleapp with old org key, update REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY in container, trigger a reconnect and assert streaming uses new_proj_456. If we do SIGHUP vs in-process export we should document which works.

Jon: Also update sampleapp README with a short paragraph about how to rotate keys in containers (restart vs env reload vs sending SIGHUP) so users don't rely on in-process exports that don't affect cached clients.

Leah: I'll take docs. Will add a tiny troubleshooting section and a short snippet showing `kubectl exec` + restart pattern.

Maya: :thumbsup: I'll validate the PR against our onboarding flow once Samir posts it.

Samir: WIP — pushing a small branch in a bit. Thanks for catching this, Maya.

Maya: Thanks team — saved us a lot of onboarding confusion.
